What are Original works and Maintenance works ?
cards.answer: Works are classified primarily as original works and repairs and maintenance. Original works cover all new construction, additions and alterations to existing works, reconstruction of entire structures after wear or calamity, and repairs to newly purchased or abandoned buildings needed to make them usable. Repairs and maintenance cover the operations needed from time to time to keep existing property in satisfactory state when complete reconstruction is not necessary, and are further divided into ordinary and special repairs.
cards.answer_source: Kerala Financial Code Vol I, Article 164

quotes.text: Original works include all new construction, whether of entirely new works or of additions and alterations to existing works, reconstruction of entire structures necessitated by wear and tear or by damage due to some calamity and all repairs to newly purchased or previously abandoned buildings required to make them usable.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Art. 164 Classification of works

quotes.text: Repairs and maintenance include all the operations required from time to time to maintain existing properties in a satisfactory state and make good the damage due to wear and tear, when complete reconstruction is not necessary.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Art. 164 Classification of works

Define “Duty” as per Kerala State Subordinate Service Rules 1958.
cards.answer: Rule 2(6) of the KS&SS Rules 1958 defines when a person is 'on duty' as a member of a service. He is on duty when he is performing the duties of a post borne on the cadre of that service, or is undergoing the probation, instruction or training prescribed for it. Joining time, authorised vacation or holidays between duty periods, deputation during probation and waiting for posting orders after reporting for duty are also treated as duty.

cards.question: Register of increment for non gazetted officers has been maintained by the drawing officers in Form No. 8 which is objected by A. G. Why ?
cards.answer: The Register of Increments is to be kept in Form 9 A, not Form 8. The drawing officer records the authorisation of each increment in it, with matching entries in the Service Book. So an objection by the Accountant General to the use of a different form is valid under the Financial Code.
cards.answer_source: Kerala Financial Code Vol I, Article 78

quotes.text: A ‘Register of Increments’ will be maintained by the drawing officer, in Form 9 A in which the authorisation of increments will be recorded by him with corresponding entries in the Service Book.
quotes.ref: Kerala Financial Code Vol I, Article 78 (Drawal of an increment in pay)

cards.answer: A Rate Contract fixes the rates at which stores are supplied during the contract period, usually without any quantity being stated. The contractor must accept any order placed within the period, and Government undertakes to buy the contracted stores from him subject to certain reservations. A Running Contract is for an approximate quantity of stores at a specified price during a period, where indenters may demand their requirements at any time and the purchaser may take about 25 per cent over or below the approximate quantity. Tenders with earnest money and performance security are compulsory for running contracts.

quotes.text: A Rate Contract is a contract for the supply of stores at specified rates during the period covered by the contract.
quotes.ref: Store Purchase Manual 2013, para 13.4

quotes.text: A Running Contract is a contract for the supply of an approximate quantity of stores at a specified price during a certain period.
quotes.ref: Store Purchase Manual 2013, para 13.2

quotes.text: It is important that for all running contracts, tenders with earnest money should be invited irrespective of the amount involved and that performance security are also furnished by the Contractors.
quotes.ref: Store Purchase Manual 2013, para 13.3

What are the general principles of allocation of expenditure between capital and revenue.
cards.answer: Article 30-A of the Kerala Account Code Vol I lays down the guiding principles. Capital expenditure is incurred to increase concrete assets of a material and permanent character, the assets must belong to the authority spending, and expenditure on a temporary asset is not capital. Capital bears first construction and equipment charges, while revenue bears later maintenance and working expenses.

quotes.text: (5) Capital should bear all charges for the first construction and equipment of a project as well as charges for intermediate maintenance of the work while not yet opened for service.
quotes.ref: KAC Vol I, Art. 30-A(5)

cards.answer: Secret service expenses are governed by Appendix 6 of KFC Vol I (referred to in Art. 103). The officer keeps a contingent register and a secret cash book, bills need no vouchers, and Government nominates a controlling officer who does an administrative audit at least once a year and certifies to the Accountant General. The accounts are not scrutinised by audit. Appropriation control (Budget Manual para 67) checks expenditure against the available budget provision at the treasury.
cards.answer_source: KFC Vol I, Appendix 6; Kerala Budget Manual para 67

quotes.text: The accounts of secret service expenditure will not be subjected to scrutiny by the audit authority.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol II, Appendix 6 para 5 Rules for secret service expenses

quotes.text: When a bill is presented for payment at the treasury, the availability of budget provision (appropriation) to cover the payment is checked with reference to the entries in the Appropriation Control Register, specially maintained for the purpose.
quotes.ref: Kerala Budget Manual, para 67 Appropriation Control

cards.question: An L.D. Clerk in Collectorate, Wayanad was on Maternity Leave till 31-12-2017. She applied for earned leave from 1-1-2018 to 1-3-2018, in continuation of Maternity leave. Her application was rejected as it was not supported by Medical certificate.
cards.answer: Maternity leave may be combined with any other kind of leave. Leave applied for in continuation of maternity leave normally needs a medical certificate, but the proviso says no certificate is needed for leave of up to sixty days in continuation. Earned leave from 1-1-2018 to 1-3-2018 is 60 days, so rejecting the application for want of a medical certificate was wrong.

quotes.text: Provided that no medical certificate shall be necessary for grant of any leave for a period not exceeding sixty days in continuation of maternity leave.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 102 (Maternity leave combined with other leave), proviso

cards.question: Provisions for pay and fixed allowances for Govt. Servants for March 2018 was not made in the Budget Estimates for 2017-18.
A contingent bill was endorsed to a private party by the drawing officer on 10-12-2017. It was presented at the treasury on 18-3-2018. The treasury officer refused the payment.
cards.answer: A contingent bill endorsed in favour of a private party is valid only for three months from the date of issue. A bill endorsed on 10-12-2017 and presented on 18-3-2018 is beyond three months, and in any case an endorsement made in the last quarter is valid only up to the end of March. The treasury officer's refusal therefore turns on the three-month limit; the payee must get the bill re-endorsed/revalidated by the drawing officer.

quotes.text: No endorsement on a contingent bill remains valid for longer than three months counting from the date of issue.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Rule 112(c) Endorsement of Contingent Bills in favour of private parties

cards.question: A treasury officer paid the honorarium sanctioned by the Public Service Commission to Gazetted officer without the authorisation of the Accountant General.
cards.answer: Normally a Treasury Officer cannot pay a reward or honorarium to a gazetted officer until the Accountant General has intimated the rate of payment. However, honorarium paid to a gazetted government servant by the Kerala Public Service Commission is a listed exception, so such payment without the Accountant General's authorisation is not irregular.
cards.answer_source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 18 and exception (b)

quotes.text: No withdrawal shall be permitted in order to meet the pay, leave salary, or allowances of a gazetted government servant or a reward or honorarium payable to a gazetted government servant
quotes.ref: KTC Vol I, Rule 18

quotes.text: (b) for payment of honorarium to gazetted government servant by the Kerala Public Service Commission.
quotes.ref: KTC Vol I, Rule 18 Exceptions (b)

cards.question: A Gazetted officer where L.P.C was issued on transfer, presented the T.A. bill for the period before his transfer in the old treasury and the Treasury officer
Permanent Advance and Temporary Advance
cards.answer: A permanent advance is a standing advance granted to a Government servant to meet unforeseen urgent expenditure before bills are drawn, limited to what is absolutely essential and recouped periodically. A temporary advance is for contingent expenditure of a specified kind or on a specific occasion, needing Government sanction (or a standing sanction) for that purpose.

quotes.text: To enable him to make disbursements of this kind before drawing the necessary bills, a Government servant may be granted a permanent advance the amount of which should be limited to what is absolutely essential to meet his ordinary requirements.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Art. 94

quotes.text: When a temporary advance is considered necessary for the purpose of meeting contingent expenditure of a specified kind or on a specific occasion and it is not covered by standing sanction given by the Government, an application for sanction should be submitted to the Government.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Art. 99 Temporary advances for specified purposes

cards.question: Treasury cash balance and currency cash chest
cards.answer: The treasury balance is the Government's cash balance held in the treasury, from which disbursements are made and into which receipts are paid. The currency chest is a separate chest ordinarily kept in the treasury; its contents belong to the Reserve Bank of India, but Government is responsible to the Bank for them and must safeguard them as carefully as the treasury balance.
cards.answer_source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Note 1 (treasury balance and currency chest balance)

quotes.text: The moneys held in a treasury as part of the Government’s cash balance form the treasury balance, from which Government disbursements are made and into which Government receipts are paid.
quotes.ref: KTC Vol I, Note 1 - Treasury balance and currency chest balance

quotes.text: The contents of the currency chest are the property of the Reserve Bank but the Government are responsible to the Reserve Bank, for them.
quotes.ref: KTC Vol I, Note 1 - Treasury balance and currency chest balance

cards.question: Appropriation and re-appropriation II (a) What are the main rules laid down to ensure that the Treasury strong room is safe
cards.answer: No place may be used as a treasury strong room unless a PWD officer not lower than an Executive Engineer certifies that it is secure and fit. Every strong room must be inspected annually by the Executive Engineer or a deputed officer, and the Treasury Officer obtains a safety certificate after each inspection. The Superintendent of Police prescribes the positions of sentries and extra precautions; the Executive Engineer is responsible for the building and the Treasury Officer for chests and furniture.
cards.answer_source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 136

quotes.text: No place should be used as a strong-room, unless an officer of the Public Works Department not lower in rank than an Executive Engineer has certified that it is secure and fit for use as a strong room.
quotes.ref: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 136(a) Treasury strong room

quotes.text: Every strong room should be inspected annually by the Executive Engineer or by an experienced Assistant Engineer or an officer holding sub divisional charge deputed by the Executive Engineer for the purpose
quotes.ref: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 136(c) Treasury strong room

For issuing a fresh cheque by a cheque drawing officer of PWD/Forest in a case where the drawing officer receives a report that a cheque drawn by him has been lost. [5] [P.T.O.
cards.answer: Under Kerala Treasury Code Rule 250 the drawing officer must at once report the loss to the Treasury Officer and ask him to stop payment. The Treasury Officer checks the paid-cheque lists and, if unpaid, stops payment and sends a non-payment certificate. On receiving the certificate the drawing officer cancels the original cheque, makes the entries in his accounts and may then issue another cheque in its place.

quotes.text: When a drawing officer receives a report that a cheque drawn by him has been lost, he shall at once report the fact to the Treasury Officer and request him to stop payment of the cheques.
quotes.ref: KTC Vol I, Rule 250 Lost cheques

quotes.text: On receipt of the certificate duly signed by the Treasury Officer the drawing officer shall cancel the original cheque and make the necessary entries in his accounts and may then issue another in its place.
quotes.ref: KTC Vol I, Rule 250 Lost cheques

cards.question: Revenue is collected in one district on account of another district and credited to the Treasury Account of the receiving district.
cards.answer: Correct. Revenue collected in one district on account of another is credited in the treasury account of the receiving district under the proper head, and the fact is intimated to the departmental officer of the district concerned.

quotes.text: Revenue collected in one district on account of another should be credited in the treasury account of the receiving district under the appropriate head of account and the fact intimated to the appropriate departmental officer in the district concerned.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Art. 8(7)(iii) Maintenance of proper accounts

cards.question: Excess over appropriation of a financial year comes to notice of the Controlling officer after closing of the financial year.
cards.answer: The department administering a grant must see that expenditure does not exceed the amount provided by the Legislature. Excess expenditure first noticed after the financial year closes is always treated as an irregularity, and where the grant as a whole is exceeded a demand for excess grant must be presented to the Legislature under Article 205 of the Constitution.

quotes.text: As such, excess expenditure which comes to notice after the expiry of the financial year is always looked upon as an irregularity.
quotes.ref: Kerala Budget Manual, Para 97(1) Excess Grant

cards.question: Substantial savings in funds allotted under a Major head for a financial year were noticed in March of that year and it was evaluated that no more funds under that head would be required to be spent before the close of that financial year. VI For what purpose (s) ...............
A revised estimate for various grants sanctioned by the Legislature are prepared ?
cards.answer: A Revised Estimate is an estimate of the probable revenue and expenditure of the current financial year framed during the year. It is based on actual transactions recorded so far plus anticipated transactions for the rest of the year, and should be prepared as realistically as possible because it guides the next year's budget estimate.
cards.answer_source: Kerala Budget Manual, Chapter II and para 20

quotes.text: Revised estimate is an estimate of the probable revenue and expenditure of the current financial year under the various heads, framed during the course of the year, based on the actual transactions so far recorded and the anticipation for the rest of the year.
quotes.ref: Kerala Budget Manual, Revised Estimate (Chapter II / para 20)

cards.question: Each disbursing officer is required to maintain a register of Expenditure and Liabilities.
cards.answer: True. Each Disbursing Officer must maintain a register of expenditure and liabilities in Form KBM 12, and report the expenditure and liabilities monthly to the superior controlling authority.

quotes.text: each disbursing Officer should maintain a register of expenditure and liabilities, in Form KBM 12.
quotes.ref: Kerala Budget Manual, Para 70(1) Disbursing Officers

cards.question: Each departmental officer is required to maintain a register of immovable properties.
cards.answer: KFC Vol I Rule 170 requires all officers to maintain permanent registers in Form 23, one for buildings and lands and one for roads, bridges and culverts. Each officer's register covers the Government immovable properties under his control and that of his subordinates. Changes must be intimated to the officers concerned and an annual certificate recorded at the end of March.

quotes.text: The permanent registers, one for buildings and lands and the other for roads, bridges and culverts, will be maintained in Form 23 (I and II) by all Officers to show the assets of Government in the form of immovable properties under their charge.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Rule 170 Maintenance of register of immovable properties

cards.question: Heads of offices, controlling officers, are required to maintain Audit objection register ? VII Comment on the following. (Relevant rules should be quoted)
cards.answer: Yes. A register in Form 4 must be maintained in each office for recording objections communicated by the Accountant General. There should be only one Audit Objection Register for the whole office, one person made responsible for it, and it is reviewed monthly by the Head of Office.

quotes.text: A register should be maintained in each office in Form 4 for recording the objections communicated by the Accountant General.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Art. 63(a)

quotes.text: There should be only one register for the whole office and a particular person in the office should be made responsible for the maintenance of the register.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Art. 63(b)(6) Maintenance and check of Audit Objection Register

cards.question: A Govt. servant who was on earned leave from 1-6-2017 to 31-7-2017 was suspended from service with effect from 10-7-2017. He was paid subsistence allowance from 1-8-2017 the date following the expiry of earned leave sanctioned.
cards.answer: For an officer on leave with allowances, an order of suspension cancels the leave for the period of suspension and he is entitled to subsistence allowance. So the subsistence allowance was due from 10-7-2017, the date of suspension, not from the day after the earned leave would have expired.

quotes.text: In the case of an Officer on leave with allowances, the orders of suspension shall have the effect of cancelling the leave for the period of suspension. He shall be entitled to subsistence allowance.
quotes.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 55B(ii)

cards.question: A Govt. servant was granted ‘Leave Not Due’ for 40 days from 1-4-2017. At the time of proceeding on LND, he was having 4 more full year service before superannuation. He expired on 5-5-2017. His drawing officer recovered the leave salary already paid to him from his dues.

Treasury officer Palakkad returned a TA bill of District collector Palakkad for an official journey made in Coimbatore District on the ground that for the said journey outside the state, no Govt. sanction is obtained.
cards.answer: Heads of Departments and District Collectors are themselves competent to sanction journeys in the public interest to adjoining districts of neighbouring States. So a District Collector's journey to Coimbatore district needs no separate Government sanction, and the treasury officer was not justified in returning the TA bill on that ground.
cards.answer_source: KSR Vol I, Part I, Chapter II (TA), Rule 47 Note 2

quotes.text: Note 2.- The Heads of Departments and District Collectors will be competent to undertake journeys outside the State in the adjoining districts of neighbouring States in public interest.
quotes.ref: KSR Vol I, Rule 47 Note 2 (Travelling Allowances, Journeys on Tour)

cards.question: A Treasury Officer permitted part payment of an earnest money deposit.
cards.answer: This is irregular. An earnest money deposit can never be repaid in part; it must be refunded in full on a proper refund order.
cards.answer_source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, refund of deposits

quotes.text: An earnest money deposit shall never be repaid in part.
quotes.ref: KTC Vol I, rule on repayment of deposits (earnest money deposit)

cards.question: A Govt. official residing in Govt. quarters in which he is bound to reside for performance of his duties put in a claim for compensation from Govt. on account of theft of some of his valuables from it. His Head of office recommended it to higher authorities for
cards.answer: Compensation will ordinarily not be granted for loss by theft. The mere fact that the official lives in Government quarters in which he is bound to reside for his duties is not sufficient ground. The claim should therefore not be admitted, although the Head of Office recommended it.

quotes.text: The mere fact that at the time of the accident, the Government servant is technically on duty or is living in Government quarters in which he is bound to reside for the performance of his duties will not be considered as a sufficient ground for the grant of compensation.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Rule 231(1)(c) Compensation for loss of property
